Siddammannamma vs Sri. Nanjundegowda on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49826538/
2 MYSURU ALLOWING THE PETITION UNDER ORDER 20 RULE 18 OF CPC.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE V SRISHANANDA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri Rupesh Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant and K.R. Krishnamurthy, learned counsel for respondent No.1 (a).
2.

Order passed in R.A.No.190/2017, whereby the order passed in FDP No.27/2011 is set aside and the matter is remitted to the Trial Court for fresh consideration after appointing a Court Commissioner to demarcate the petition property is assailed in this second appeal.
3. Parties are referred to as plaintiff and defendant for sake of convenience as per their original ranking before the Trial Court.
4. Facts which are not in dispute are that a suit for partition is filed by the plaintiff which was decreed by granting a 2/7th share to the plaintiff and collectively 5/7th share to the defendants.
Admittedly, there was no challenge to the preliminary decree and Final Decree Proceedings were initiated in FDP No.27/2011.

6. Learned Judge in the Trial Court after notifying the parties, allowed the Final Decree Proceedings and demarcated the portion of the property based on the commissioner's report, appointed and plaintiff was allotted 12 guntas of land in the petition property in Sy.No.19/1 of Lalithadripura village, Varuna Hobli, Mysore Taluk, which was shown in red colour in the commissioner's report and another 12 guntas of land which was shown in the green colour in the commissioner's sketch.
Said division was subject matter of the appeal before the First Appellate Court in R.A No.190/2017.

7. Learned Judge in the First Appellate Court secured the records and heard the parties and after hearing the parties, the learned Judge in the First Appellate Court found that the Trial Court committed an error in allotting 12 guntas of the land as aforesaid in favour of the plaintiff and set aside the order.

8. In paragraph 16 to 19, the learned Judge in the First Appellate Court has held as under:
Smt. Siddammannamma vs Sri. Nanjundegowda on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49826538/
3 NC: 2024:KHC:37772 "16.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead of doing this, the Court Commissioner has prepared the sketch for entire extent of 2 Acres 6 Guntas of the Sy.No.19/1 and in the said sketch, he has shown 38 guntas in Blue Colour as having been acquired for Ring Road, 8  guntas in Orange Colour and 5 Guntas in Yellow Colour to have been formed into road and shown the remaining portions of 12 Guntas each in Green and Red Colours to be the vacant land available and 6 guntas in Black Colour is shown to have been formed into sites by the appellant's society.
On this basis, the Court Commissioner has opined that 12 guntas of vacant land shown in Red Colour can be allotted to respondent No.1 and this has been accepted by the court below.

17. The basic error in this approach is that, it is not clear whether 12 guntas of land which has been allotted to respondent No.1 falls within 1 acre 2 guntas which is the petition schedule property.
This is because, the Commissioner has not at all demarcated and identified the petition schedule property of 1 Acre 2 Guntas.

18. Without appreciating this fact, the court below committed an error in simply accepting the Commissioner's Report and granting said 12 guntas of land to respondent No.1 without first ascertaining whether said 12 guntas of land is the part of 1 Acre 2 guntas of petition schedule property or not.
19.
The court below has held that the petition schedule property measures 1 acre 2 guntas and 2/7th share therein comes to 12 guntas and on this premise allotted 12 guntas to respondent No.1.

At this stage, it is relevant to refer to the findings of the court below in its order dated 20.12.2014 NC: 2024:KHC:37772 while rejecting second Commissioner's Report wherein the court below has observed as follows:-
Para 17: Further, in this case, there is a subsequent event of acquisition of the suit property by the Mysuru Urban Development Authority for formation of Ring Road as well as service road.
If the entire land is available for division by 07 equal shares, the plaintiff would be entitled for 12 guntas.

When the entire land is not available for partition in view of the subsequent acquisition of land by Mysuru Urban Development Authority for formation of Ring Road as well as Service Road, the Report of the Commissioner by demarcating 12 guntas to the plaintiff alone is contrary to the law as well as the Preliminary Decree.

As per the Preliminary Decree,
not only the plaintiff, but also the other sharers are also entitled for an extent of 12 guntas if entire land is available for partition. When the CW1/Commissioner is one breath has deposed that the plaintiff is entitled for 12 guntas, in another beach he has deposed that she is entitled for 6 guntas only.
His evidence is also full of confusions and he is not certain about the exact extent available for partition.
His evidence is also contrary to his report marked as Ex.C2.

If his Report is accepted, it is detrimental to the interests of other co- sharers, more particularly for defendants 3 and 4, since they have also prayed for carving out of their shares by paying court fee.
Hence, the report of the Commissioner cannot be accepted."

Smt. Siddammannamma vs Sri. Nanjundegowda on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49826538/
4 (Emphasis supplied) NC: 2024:KHC:37772
The reason for extracting extensively the said observations of the lower court is that, afore stated orders has attained finality.
The Court below n the said orders has correctly observed that, if the entire land is available for division, then respondent No.1 would be entitled to 12 guntas of land.
However, entire land is not available in view of some portions of the land having been acquired for Ring Road.

Therefore, it was for the Court Commissioner to identify 1 Acre 2 Guntas of land which is the petition schedule property and then ascertain how much of that land has been acquired for formation of Ring Road and only then, the land which can be allotted to respondent No.1 can be determined.

Without adverting to this aspect of the matter, the lower court committed an error in blindly accepting the Commissioner's Report and allotting 12 guntas to respondent No.1, by the impugned judgment."

9. Learned Judge in the First Appellate Court in the impugned judgment also noted that there was an acquisition proceeding by Mysuru Urban Development Authority and there is a purchase of a property from one of the sharers and objections raised in the objection statement has not been properly considered by the learned Trial Judge.

10. The learned Judge in the First Appellate Court also felt that a fresh Commissioner needs to be appointed as portion of 1 acre 2 guntas in Sy.No.19/1 of the suit properties has been NC:
2024:KHC:37772 acquired by Mysuru Urban Development Authority.
Therefore, the parties are entitled for compensation for the acquired portion and in the remaining portion the shares are to be carved out as per the Preliminary Decree.
11. Without such an exercise, accepting the Commissioner report has thus resulted in injustice.

Therefore, the lerned Judge in First Appellate Court was justified in setting aside the order passed by the Trial Court and directed the fresh Court Commissioner to measure the remaining land after the giving deduction to the land acquired by the Mysuru Urban Development Authority in 1 acre 2 guntas of land in Sy.No.19/1 and demarcated their respective shares.
12.
Accordingly, this Court does not find any infirmity in such an order of the First Appellate Court calling any interference by acting under Order XLIII CPC vested in this Court.

Hence, the following :
ORDER Appeal is dismissed.

Parties shall appear before the Trial Court on 30.09.2024 and thereafter the Trial Court is directed to proceed with the matter in accordance with law as per the directions of the First Appellate Court.
